top_choice_rationale: P001 awards the optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye. The magic-wavelength condition cancels the dominant trapping light shift so many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once, and the systematic-shift budgets (blackbody radiation, lattice hyperpolarisability, collisions) have been reproduced independently at about 1e-18. The two names map onto distinct contributions (concept and first strontium realisation; record accuracy and many-body regimes), and a citation naming the lattice clock specifically separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. No award would withhold a mature, well-attributed achievement.
recusal_note: No specific conflict with Katori or Ye is apparent from my profile; my documented collaborators (L'Huillier, Keller's group, Schuch, Dahlstrom, Argenti, Indelicato) are not among the credited names, though my field of theoretical atomic physics is close to precision atomic measurement.
